description: Returns snapshots of one market, oldest first. Each row has time, spot_price, price_up, and price_down. Use it for tick detail in a short time range. For the shape of a whole market, use polytest_get_price_series. A market has about 8 snapshots per second, so narrow the range with start_time and end_time. With include_orderbook each row also has the Up and Down order books, cut to orderbook_depth levels per side, and a page holds at most 20 rows. The book at one moment is this tool with start_time set to that moment, limit 1, and include_orderbook true. Costs 1 API request. To continue, call again with offset set to next_offset while stop is "more". stop "snapshot_offset_cap" means offsets end at 100000, so move start_time forward to continue. If truncated is true, rows were cut to keep the result small and next_offset points at the first cut row.

end_time.description: ISO 8601. Keeps snapshots at or before this time. No zone means UTC.

include_orderbook.description: Adds the Up and Down order books to each row.

limit.description: Rows per page. At most 20 with order books.

market_id.description: PolyTest market id from polytest_list_markets or polytest_get_market.

offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass next_offset from the previous page.

orderbook_depth.description: Price levels kept per side of each book.

start_time.description: ISO 8601. Keeps snapshots at or after this time. No zone means UTC.

name: polytest_get_snapshots

next_offset.description: Offset of the next page when stop is more.

price_down.description: Lowest ask on the Down order book, 0 to 1: what buying Down cost at that moment. Null when nobody was selling Down. Up and Down asks usually add up to a little more than 1.

price_up.description: Lowest ask on the Up order book, 0 to 1: what buying Up cost at that moment. Null when nobody was selling Up.

truncated.description: True when rows were cut to keep the result small.

title: Get snapshots
